data.gender_notes: Idona is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Ida was a mountain nymph associated with childbirth and fertility. The name Idaona is derived from this goddess and carries the same symbolism. The name Idona carries the meaning “Goddess of fertility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Idona usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Idona belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of fertility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Idona total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Idaona holds a rich cultural significance, rooted in Greek mythology. As a derivative of the Greek goddess Ida, it is associated with the revered mountain associated with childbirth and fertility. This name carries the ethereal allure of old Greek folklore and mythology, evoking images of sacred sites, divine initiation, and the power of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: Idaona embodies the essence of creativity, transformation, and new beginnings. Spiritually, the name suggests the cycle of life, birth, and renewal, and is believed to represent the energy of compassion, nurturing, and the power to overcome challenges. For Christians or those with a spiritual leaning towards Greek mythology, wearing or using the name Idaona may serve as a source of inspiration, strength, and renewed faith. May its rich symbolism bring a sense of peace, growth, and adventure into one's life.
